title: Best tools to create a business case for a sale (2026)
summary: The best tools to create a business case for a sale in 2026, compared: AI agents that generate the case for you, value-selling platforms, and document builders.
body_text: Last updated: July 2026 The best tools to create a business case for a sale in 2026 are Mutiny, Mediafly, Ecosystems, Cuvama, and PandaDoc. Here is the quick version of who each one is for: Mutiny — best overall for teams that want the full, personalized business case generated for them in minutes and tied to the rest of the deal. Mediafly — best for enterprise value-selling programs run by a dedicated value team. Ecosystems — best when you want the buyer to co-build the value assessment with you. Cuvama — best for tying the value case directly to sales discovery. PandaDoc — best for turning a finished case into a signable proposal document. The biggest difference between these tools is how much of the case each one writes for you. Mutiny generates the problem, the cost of inaction, the ROI, and the narrative for the specific account. The value-selling platforms focus on the ROI math, and the document tools format the final proposal. This guide covers what a business case is, why it decides deals, the types of tools, what to look for, the five best options, and how to generate one. What is a business case in sales? A sales business case is a short, buyer-specific document that justifies a purchase. It states the problem, quantifies the cost of inaction, lays out the proposed solution, and shows the expected ROI and payback for that account. It is the artifact a champion uses to win internal approval, so it has to make the argument on its own without the rep in the room. The business case is also a core component of a deal room, and it often anchors the sales pitch deck. Why does a strong business case matter? A business case decides whether a deal moves or dies, because most buyers require one and most stalled deals stall on justification. Per Forrester, 97% of B2B buyers build a business case to justify their purchases. When the case for change is weak, buyers default to doing nothing: Challenger found that 40% to 60% of lost deals end in no decision rather than a loss to a competitor. The pressure is higher because buyers self-serve. According to Gartner, B2B buyers spend only 17% of the purchase journey with suppliers, and Gartner’s 2025 survey found 61% prefer a rep-free experience. A business case that stands on its own carries the deal through the parts of the journey the rep never sees. Types of business case tools The tools fall into four categories, from most to least hands-off on the actual writing: AI business case generators: create the full, account-specific case (problem, cost of inaction, ROI, and narrative) from your CRM and call context. Mutiny leads here. Value-selling and ROI platforms: quantify ROI and TCO through calculators and value assessments, usually run by a value or enablement team. Mediafly and Ecosystems sit here. Discovery-to-value tools: turn sales discovery into a structured value case. Cuvama sits here. Document and proposal builders: format and e-sign the finished case. PandaDoc sits here. Most categories still leave the rep to write the narrative. The AI generator category is the one that produces a finished, personalized case a champion can forward. What should you look for in a business case tool? Look for four things: how much of the case the tool creates for you, how well it personalizes to the account, whether any rep can use it without a value team, and whether it connects to the rest of the deal. Content generation: does it draft the full case, or only the ROI numbers? Personalization: can it tailor the case to the specific account automatically? Self-serve usability: can any rep build one, or does it need a dedicated value or enablement team? Connected workflow: does the case tie into the deal room, pricing, and follow-ups, or live in a silo? The 5 best tools to create a business case for a sale 1. Mutiny Mutiny is the top-rated AI tool for creating personalized deal content and GTM workflow automation. For business cases, Mutiny generates the whole case itself: the problem, the cost of inaction, the ROI, and the narrative built for the specific account, in minutes. It runs as a two-sided model. The agent creates the customer-facing case, and reps and marketers build their own agents and routines to automate the busywork around the deal, from follow-ups to keeping the numbers current. Any AE, BDR, marketer, or CSM can run it on day one with no GTM engineer or value team required, starting from a pre-built business case blueprint. Sales leaders can standardize that blueprint so every rep runs the same play. Best for: teams that want the full business case generated and tied to the rest of the deal. Pricing: Free, Business, and Enterprise custom plans (starting at $30k). “Generating something in one shot rather than 100 iterations, that’s the [Mutiny] difference.” Basten Heutink, Chief of Staff, Delphi 2. Mediafly Mediafly is a revenue enablement suite with a value-selling module that provides ROI and TCO calculators and business value assessments. It is strong for enterprise value-selling programs, and it is typically run by an enablement or value team that builds and governs the value tools reps use. Best for: enterprise value-selling programs managed by a dedicated value team. 3. Ecosystems Ecosystems is a collaborative value management platform where a seller and buyer build a value assessment together. It formalizes value selling and keeps the quantified value front and center through the deal and into customer success. Best for: teams that want buyers to co-build the value assessment. 4. Cuvama Cuvama is an AI discovery-to-value-case platform that connects sales discovery to a champion-ready value case. It turns what the rep learns in discovery into a structured “why buy, why now, why us” case grounded in ROI. Best for: teams that want the value case tied directly to discovery. 5. PandaDoc PandaDoc is a document and proposal platform with e-signature. It is useful for turning a finished business case into a polished, signable document, with templates and approval workflows on the contract side of the deal. Best for: turning the business case into a signable proposal document. Tool Best for Approach to the business case Mutiny Generating the full case and connecting it to the deal AI drafts the problem, cost of inaction, ROI, and narrative per account; reps automate the surrounding workflow Mediafly Enterprise value-selling programs ROI and TCO calculators run by a value team Ecosystems Buyer-collaborative value selling Value assessments co-built with the buyer Cuvama Discovery-driven value cases Connects discovery to a champion-ready value case PandaDoc Signable proposal documents Document templates and e-signature How do you generate a business case for a sale? At a high level: state the problem in the buyer’s words, quantify the cost of inaction, lay out the solution, show the ROI with clear assumptions, and end with a recommendation and next step. For the step-by-step walkthrough, see how to build a business case for a B2B deal, or start from a business case template. For the component list, see what a sales business case should include. The fastest path is to generate the case rather than write it by hand. With Mutiny, a rep starts from the business case blueprint and the agent generates the personalized case in minutes, so the first draft exists before the rep would otherwise have finished the math. See how account executives use Mutiny to build deal-ready cases without waiting on a value team.

title: What Is an International Payment Gateway? A Beginner’s Guide
summary: Learn how a payment gateway for international payments works, how to accept international payments in India, key features to compare, and how to choose the right solution for your business.
body_text: Table of Contents Toggle Expanding your business globally means making it easy for overseas customers to pay you. Whether you’re a freelancer, exporter, SaaS company, or ecommerce brand, you’ll need a payment gateway for international payments to securely accept transactions from customers across different countries and currencies. An international payment gateway does more than process payments. It enables businesses to accept international cards, supports multiple currencies, handles currency conversion, and complies with both Indian and global payment regulations. With the right solution, Indian businesses can sell globally while offering a seamless checkout experience. But what an international payment gateway is, how it works, its key features, and what to consider when choosing the best payment gateway for international transactions. Let’s break it all down. What Are International Transactions? International transactions refer to the exchange of goods, services, or funds between individuals or businesses in different countries. For example, an Indian exporter shipping products to Europe, a SaaS company billing customers in the US, or a freelancer receiving payments from clients overseas are all examples of international transactions. Unlike domestic payments, cross-border transactions involve multiple currencies, banking networks, exchange rates, and country-specific regulations. A reliable payment gateway to accept international payments in India simplifies these complexities by securely processing payments, managing currency conversion, and ensuring regulatory compliance. What Is an International Payment Gateway? An international payment gateway is a secure online payment system that enables businesses to accept and process transactions from customers across the globe. Unlike a domestic gateway that only supports local cards and currency, an international gateway is designed for cross-border commerce. Accept payments in multiple currencies Process international debit and credit cards Support global wallets and payment methods Handle currency conversion Meet RBI and international compliance requirements Settle payments directly into an Indian bank account In short, it enables Indian businesses to accept payments from customers worldwide while delivering a secure and frictionless payment experience. How Does a Payment Gateway for International Payments Work? When an overseas customer makes a purchase from your website, an international payment gateway securely processes the transaction behind the scenes. Here’s how the process works: Customer Checkout: The customer selects a product or service and pays using an international credit card, debit card, or supported digital wallet. Payment Authorization: The payment gateway encrypts the transaction details and securely sends them to the customer’s issuing bank for approval. Currency Conversion: If the customer pays in a foreign currency, the gateway processes the exchange rate and converts the amount before settlement. Transaction Approval: Once the issuing bank verifies the payment, the transaction is approved or declined based on available funds and security checks. Settlement: The approved payment is processed through international banking networks and settled into the merchant’s Indian bank account, usually within a few business days. Reporting & Compliance: The gateway provides transaction reports, settlement details, and required documentation to help businesses manage accounting and regulatory requirements. The entire process takes only a few seconds for customers while ensuring secure and compliant cross-border payment processing . Common Types of International Payments Businesses use international payment gateways for a variety of cross-border transactions, including: Retail and Service Sales: E-commerce, consulting, software, all billed globally. Education and Events: Online tutoring, webinars, and digital courses with overseas participants. Subscription and SaaS: Monthly or annual plans for clients abroad. Remittances: Individuals sending money for personal or family needs. Export payments Whether you’re selling physical products or digital services, an international payment gateway helps streamline payment collection from customers worldwide. Key Features of an International Payment Gateway When evaluating a payment gateway for international payments, look for these essential features: Multi-Currency Support: The payment system should be capable of accepting payments in over 100 global currencies; this way, customers can pay in the currency they are most comfortable with. Meanwhile, your dashboard displays the settled INR or the currency of your choice. Wide, Ranging Payment Methods: The platform should facilitate the use of international cards (Visa, MasterCard, Amex), global wallets (PayPal, Apple Pay), and the alternative payment methods that are most relevant to the buyers residing overseas. Dynamic Currency Conversion (DCC) : Allow customers to specify their home currency and make payments with full transparency, thereby lessening the points of contact and increasing the chances of getting conversions. Localized Checkout: A checkout process would be more efficient with local language support, allowing the checkout pages to appear in the language of the local consumers, coupled with local checkout patterns. PCI DSS & Global Security Compliance: The presence of end to end encryption, tokenization, & 3D secure features assists in securing each & every transaction. Fraud Detection: Smarter anti-fraud tools, fueled by Artificial Intelligence, and flexible risk engines that have learned from global trends. Developer, Friendly Integration: Well-equipped with APIs, SDKs, plug-and-play modules for the most popular commerce stacks, such as Shopify, WooCommerce, amongst others. Real Time Analytics: Combined dashboards which give real insights into real processes of sales & reconcilements in domestic as well as international refunds. Instant Onboarding and No-Code Tools: From your own dashboard, the ability to immediately start accepting payments worldwide without the hassle of complicated coding and paperwork is possible. These features help businesses provide a secure, reliable, and seamless payment experience for customers across different countries. Common Challenges of Accepting International Payments ​​Expanding abroad carries real obstacles, such as prolonged settlement cycles, losses during foreign currency exchange, complicated regulations, or the danger of fraud and/or chargeback losses. Visionary international gateways mitigate such issues by: Providing T+2 or T+3 settlement cycles, so companies get payments faster. Fixing transparent and competitive exchange rates accessible to both buyers and sellers Making FIRS & compliance processes automated for peace of mind Applying universal anti-fraud techniques in all transactions This helps businesses, individuals, and young entrepreneurs to venture easily into other markets without worrying about any limitations being created either technologically or financially. Integrating an International Payment Gateway Modern payment gateways are designed for businesses of all sizes, making integration simple even without extensive technical expertise. Most providers offer: Plugins for Shopify , WooCommerce, Magento, and other ecommerce platforms APIs and SDKs for custom websites and mobile apps No-code payment links and hosted checkout pages Dashboards to manage settlements, refunds, and reports This allows businesses to start accepting international payments quickly while delivering a smooth checkout experience. How to Choose the Best Payment Gateway for International Transactions Entering new markets around the world generates new income sources; however, there are also new complexities, particularly regarding securing funds more quickly. Choosing the international payment gateway has to integrate properly with how people pay in different countries around the world and how you want to manage your operations in the background. Here are a few key factors to help guide the decision: Coverage of Currencies and Local Payment Options: Customers are more likely to complete purchases when they can pay in their own currency and use familiar methods. A good gateway should support multi-currency transactions and give access to local payment options. This can include cards, e-wallets, and money transfer solutions that are common practice within a certain region. For example, support for UPI in India or SEPA in Europe can make a noticeable difference in conversion rates. Global Compliance and Regulatory Alignment: International payments are processed under various taxation laws and privacy regulations, and protection against fraud in each country. Look for a provider that handles regional compliance requirements like PSD2, SCA, and local tax calculations, so you don’t run into trouble managing cross-border transactions. Fraud Protection and Risk Tools: Global payments bring higher fraud exposure, so built-in protection is key. Look for gateways with real-time detection, adaptive risk scoring, and customizable rules. Cashfree offers RiskShield , which helps flag suspicious disbursals using pattern analysis and rule-based filters. It’s especially useful for businesses managing vendor payouts or high-volume transactions. Transparent Pricing and Fee Structure: International transactions will have extra charges for things like currency exchange fees and international card network fees. Be sure to ask for a full quotation of the charges involved. Compare the charges of the payment services when it comes to refund charges, chargeback fees , and the time taken for payouts. Cashfree— International Payment Gateway for Ambitious Indian Brands While the world of payment gateways is crowded, a few have built deep expertise specifically focused on Indian businesses scaling into global markets. Cashfree stands out with its suite of cross-border solutions, built to offer the features growing ventures actually need. Broad Currency Support: Supports payments in 140+ currencies, with settlement in Card and leading International Wallets automatically in Indian Rupees. title: DoorDash Integrates Directly with Shopify to Connect Brick-and-Mortar Retailers with On-Demand Delivery
summary: A first-of-its-kind integration lets independent retailers get their products to consumers on demand — launching in the U.S., with international expansion planned in the months ahead.
body_text: Local businesses are the backbone of their communities. Today, we're making it easier than ever for them to reach consumers nearby. DoorDash is announcing an integration that gives independent Shopify retailers a direct, seamless path to integrate with DoorDash through the tools they already use every day. In our recent Economic Impact Report, 90% of merchants say DoorDash has helped them reach new consumers they otherwise wouldn't have been able to reach, while 85% of consumers say DoorDash makes it easier to support local businesses in their community. DoorDash is now available as a native sales channel inside Shopify's App Store — meaning any Shopify merchants with a brick-and-mortar presence in the US can add their product catalog to the DoorDash marketplace by enabling a new channel, with no separate onboarding process, manual catalog uploads, or disruption to existing operations. For consumers, this means more local stores and more delivery options in your neighborhood, available on demand. "If it's in your area, it's on DoorDash. That's the promise driving today's news. Local, independent retailers are the heart of local commerce, and they deserve tools that work as hard as they do," said Mike Goldblatt, Vice President of Enterprise Partnerships at DoorDash. "As the first on-demand marketplace that Shopify merchants can activate directly from their existing Shopify Admin, we're opening the door to retail merchants who can now reach their communities faster than ever." “Merchants want to sell wherever their customers are, and increasingly that means meeting them with speed and convenience,” said Atlee Clark, Vice President of Partnerships at Shopify. "This integration puts local retailers in front of millions of DoorDash shoppers and turns same-day demand into sales, all managed inside Shopify.” For retailers: Merchants keep their existing workflow. No changes to existing workflows. Shopify merchants extend their reach to DoorDash consumers without leaving the platform they already rely on. Go live in days, not weeks: Self-serve integration onboarding is built directly into the Shopify experience, cutting setup time from weeks to days. Products and inventory stay in sync automatically — so when a customer orders, what's on DoorDash always matches what's on the shelf. No duplicate data entry, no manual updates when stock changes. Merchants manage their catalog in Shopify, and it reflects on DoorDash in real time, keeping products moving to customers as fast as possible. From a neighborhood gift shop and a local sporting goods store to a specialty food retailer, local businesses can now tap into on-demand delivery and discovery on DoorDash without the operational burden that used to come with it. This partnership means real impact for merchants and local communities. Install the DoorDash Sales Channel App here .
